findings.problem: The request asks for a note on each confirmation, but only `confirm_element` records a reason. `confirm_wording_fix` (agent) and `confirm_all_proposed` (owner, bulk) also move elements to confirmed and take no reason. Elements confirmed those ways have an empty `confirm_reason`. `confirm_all_proposed` also cannot set a per-element reason, because it has no target Element. Later readers still can't tell why those elements were accepted.
findings.where: SKILL.md Actions: confirm_wording_fix and confirm_all_proposed; Element.confirm_reason

findings.problem: `reason` is now a required param on `confirm_element`, but `confirm_reason` is declared optional on Element. Nothing stops an empty or blank reason, so the stated goal (a note on every confirmation) isn't enforced. No precondition or invariant ties confirmed review to an existing `confirm_reason`.
findings.where: SKILL.md Element.confirm_reason and Invariants; confirm_element params

findings.problem: The world fixture E2 is already confirmed (review confirmed) but has no `confirm_reason`. That is the state the change was meant to prevent, and E1 is the only example that covers the new field. The fixtures and examples now disagree with the claim that confirmed elements carry a reason.

`confirm_element` sets `confirm_reason` before the kernel call, and the Effects text does not say what happens if the kernel call fails. The reason could then be stored on an element that never became confirmed. The reason can also be left over from an earlier attempt on elements in the unknown state.
